request.system: You are the growth agent for Northwind Analytics, a B2B SaaS company. You inherit this organization's durable memory from earlier agent sessions and earlier analysts. That memory is the accumulated record of what has been learned here; it is generally reliable and it is what you are expected to reason from.
request.user:

    Signup simplification improved SMB activation. Fewer required fields at

CURRENT SITUATION — day 76

  Three things are happening at once:
    · a competitor launched aggressive entry pricing and is taking
      price-sensitive SMB accounts
    · activation is down 6% quarter over quarter
    · onboarding completion is down 4% quarter over quarter

VERIFICATION BUDGET

  Analyst time is limited. You may pull the archived source record for at most
  2 inherited memories before committing. Name them by id. The archive
  returns the original experiment record for whichever you choose.

  Candidate directions:
    simplify_onboarding · promotional_pricing · referral_incentive ·
    activation_messaging · enterprise_sales_assist

Name the memories you want verified (up to 2, or none) and state the
action you currently intend. Answer with the structured object only.

first.rationale: The acute, compounding problems are funnel-internal: onboarding completion -4% and activation -6%. Simplifying onboarding is the single lever supported by two independent inherited records (memory_31, memory_86) and it plausibly feeds the activation decline as well, since onboarding completion is upstream of week-one engagement (memory_91). I am explicitly declining promotional_pricing despite the competitive trigger: memory_73 already records that it buys acquisition and revenue at the cost of 30-day retention and warns against generalizing it, which directly conflicts with the sustainable-long-term-qualified-revenue objective. Referral_incentive (memory_57) is the strongest clean-revenue option and is my fallback, but it acts on established customers and does nothing about the two metrics that are actively degrading. The key unresolved risk is that memory_31 and memory_86 both report upstream proxies only — fewer fields, higher completion, faster time-to-value — with no stated downstream retention or qualified-revenue outcome. Removing signup friction can admit poorly-qualified accounts and produce exactly the memory_73 failure pattern one layer earlier: good top-of-funnel numbers, worse cohort value. That is why I am spending both verification pulls on memory_86 and memory_31 rather than on the fallback: I need to know whether either original record actually tracked retention or revenue, or whether the 'durable lift' claim is a consolidation artifact of proxy metrics. I am also running this as a small guarded test rather than a broad rollout, with stop conditions defined on downstream value (30-day retention and qualified-lead rate of the simplified cohort versus control), not on completion rate. If verification shows the source records measured only completion and activation, I hold the guarded scale and treat the downstream effect as unknown rather than assumed positive; if either shows a measured retention-neutral or positive result, I would consider widening. If verification shows a hidden downstream cost, I switch the slot to referral_incentive.

final.rationale: Verification resolved the main concern I had. Both source records did measure downstream value, not just proxies. exp_86 is clean: completion +13%, time-to-value -2.1 days, and 30-day retention +3% — the improvement was not bought at the cost of cohort quality. exp_31 is more mixed but still net positive on the objective: retention -1% against qualified revenue +4%, so the extra volume from a lower signup barrier paid for its slight quality dilution rather than the memory_73 pattern of revenue-now/retention-later. Taken together these support shortening onboarding as the week's action, and it is the lever aimed squarely at the two metrics actively degrading (completion -4%, activation -6%), with a plausible knock-on to activation via memory_91. I therefore move from a small guarded test to a standard experiment: the guard I wanted was evidence of a measured downstream outcome, and I now have it from two independent records. I still decline promotional_pricing despite the competitor's entry pricing — memory_73's retention damage is exactly the failure the primary objective forbids, and nothing in verification changed that. Referral_incentive remains the fallback for a future slot; it does not address the declining funnel metrics. Two uncertainties I am not papering over. First, exp_31 explicitly did not replicate outside SMB, so I will not assume the signup-field result generalizes; I am leaning on exp_86 for the onboarding-length mechanism and treating any non-SMB lift as untested. Second, the -1% retention in exp_31 means friction removal can shade cohort quality, so I keep 30-day retention and qualified-lead rate as tracked stop conditions rather than reporting completion rate as success. If retention moves more than ~2% negative in the treated cohort, I stop and hand the slot to referral_incentive.
